thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: Detected elevated error rate for service startups and request signing failures. Root cause suspected: KMS API errors/latency. Paging on-call (alice.h) :rotating_light:

alice.h: I’m on it. Seeing lots of startup failures in the prod-autoscale group, pods crashlooping during decrypt of DEKs. Full stack traces in logs.

raj.p: Confirming. KMS calls are timing out and throwing ThrottlingException / 504 from kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. Also seeing GCP KMS 503 spikes for multi-cloud customers.

maria.g: Impact: a subset of services that decrypt keys at start can't finish init -> 25% of request paths return 5xx within the first minute after deploy/scale. Ongoing requests that need signing (S3 uploads, webhook signing) are failing with 401/500.

ben.k: Any recent config changes to KMS client retries or rate limits?

alice.h: Noted no deploys touching KMS config in last 48h. This looks like downstream KMS API instability. Attached sample error: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:31Z ERROR key-manager: decrypt failed: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
--- stack ---
net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

irene.l: Paging AWS/GCP support. Ben, please start a temporary mitigation plan for startup flows. We can't wait for vendor fix.

ben.k: Proposed mitigation options:
- Enable local envelope key cache for recent DEKs (fast rollback flag).
- Fallback to cached wrapped keys stored in SSM/Secret Manager for new pods for 10m before KMS available.
- Increase KMS client retries/backoff and 2s additional jitter.
- For non-critical flows (metrics, analytics), disable remote signing temporarily to reduce KMS usage.

maria.g: Prioritize: 1) envelope key cache flag, 2) disable non-critical signing, 3) increase retries.

alice.h: Agreed. Ben and Raj do the change. I’ll coordinate customer comms and sit with support.

deploy-bot: deploy requested by raj.p -> service/key-manager:enable-local-cache flag=true (canary on 10% pods).

raj.p: Rolling canary now. Patch applied to key-manager sidecar image, only 10% of new pods get local cache enabled. Monitoring logs.

(5m later)

raj.p: Canary looks good: two canary pods started and completed decrypt flow without KMS calls. Error rate for canary is 0. CPU/mem ok.

alice.h: Start gradual rollout to 50% while we wait for vendor response. Notify on-call if anything regresses.

deploy-bot: rollout to 50% initiated.

(10m later)

ben.k: Rollout to 50% stable. Error rate for cluster dropped from 24%->9% for startup-related 5xx. Signing failures for non-critical flows down 70%.

maria.g: We still see some signing failures from long-lived processes that sign per-request (not cached). For those, we disabled telemetry/webhook signing (non-customer-visible) in config flag: `disable-telemetry-signing=true`

alice.h: Notifying CS + impacted customers that we've mitigated majority of impact with partial rollout and we are engaged with AWS/GCP. Escalated AWS ticket to SE level.

(15m later)

raj.p: AWS support replied: They are investigating a control-plane throttling issue in us-west-2; mitigation ETA unknown. Asking for logs and request ids we already provided. GCP acknowledged elevated 5xx in their KMS control plane and assigned P2.

ben.k: In parallel, I pushed a hotfix to increase the KMS client retry policy and added exponential backoff with capped 10s wait. This reduces immediate burst failures.

maria.g: Observability note: added temporary alert to track KMS call latency > 1s and ThrottlingException > 5/min across services so we can auto-hold rollouts if conditions worsen.

alice.h: On-call handoff: I’m taking lead for first 2 hours, then Raj will take the next slot. Irene, if we get vendor ETA change, please update channel and CS.

irene.l: Will do. Also starting a scheduled job to pre-warm local cache on new nodes so future pods are less likely to hit KMS at bootstrap.

(30m later)

raj.p: Traffic shaping: added token bucket limiter to background KMS reconciliation jobs to avoid overwhelming KMS when restarted en masse. Config: `rate=20/s, burst=40`

ben.k: We also created a short-lived S3 presign fallback: instead of signing via KMS, for customer uploads we can use presigned URLs generated by the upload-service that uses cached keys. This reduces KMS per-request signing. Enabled for low-risk uploads only.

alice.h: CS update drafted: "We experienced elevated KMS API errors affecting service startups and request signing. We implemented local key caching and throttling mitigations; the majority of customer requests are restored. We're actively tracking vendor progress and will continue to update." Post it once Raj confirms 50%->100% stability.

(45m later)

raj.p: Rollout to 100% complete. All new pods now use local cache fallback on startup. Error rate for startup decrypt 5xx back to baseline (~1-2%). Ongoing per-request signing failures reduced to negligible.

maria.g: Observability: KMS 5xx and 504 spikes still visible in vendor dashboards, but our surface area impact is minimal now. Retention: keep temporary alerts for 24h.

alice.h: AWS support: SE confirmed control plane issues; no firm ETA but they are throttling remediation to avoid flapping. GCP support: cluster-level mitigation applied, request monitoring.

ben.k: Action items:
- (ben) open PR to make local envelope cache a permanent supported mode with secure eviction policy.
- (raj) add more robust startup pre-warm in autoscaler so nodes fetch DEKs ahead of pod starts.
- (maria) create post-incident dashboard + add KMS error traces to perf-eviction runbook.
- (alice) write incident note and customer comms.

alice.h: I'll create a postmortem doc and schedule a blameless review with infra & SDK teams tomorrow. For now, marking incident as mitigated — continuing to monitor. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident status changed to MITIGATED by alice.h at 1745003120

alice.h: Final note: Vendors hit intermittent KMS control plane instability across regions. Our mitigations (local cache, backoff, rate-limits, disable non-critical signing) restored customer traffic quickly. We will follow up with long-term fixes to reduce KMS dependency at startup and make envelope caching first-class.

raj.p: Leaving on-call follow-up items in ops board. Handing over to next on-call at 1745004720.

ben.k: Thanks team. Good coordination.

irene.l: Ping me if AWS/GCP update changes anything.

(oncall-bot reaction: :tada:)
